Alcohol while more physically addictive and more dangerous to detox from than most major drugs has been around for so long it makes people think it's safe.

The first mentions of marijuanna use was in China around 2700BC. It's use was common in the Far East, Middle East and even with the U.S. colonists. Carefully crafted religious/industrial smear campaigns destroyed its image over the course of 200 years or so.

Most knowledgeable people consider alcohol one of the worst drugs. Top five in harm to self and typically the worst when factoring harm to others as well. Why it's legal while others are not is a much more interesting debate.

I don't think so. After all, the earliest recorded use of marijuana is about 3,000BCE, opium's earliest use is about 1,500BCE, and cocaine's earliest known use starts about a thousand years ago.

I think the problem is that, in America, we started off with very puritanical ideas about what people should be like. The crux of the social issue with drugs, in my experience, is that people are "feeling good" even though they haven't done anything to deserve to feel good. This is why it's seen as a blight: the very hardcore people who particularly insist that the drug war is a Good Thing, that still think it's fine that marijuana is illegal even though over half of all prisoners in the US are in for non-violent possession offenses.

Alcohol doesn't really 'fit the bill' like cocaine, or marijuana, or even really opium. It makes you feel shitty, it makes you present yourself as a poorly assembled person, and the effects of addictive withdrawal from it are very tough. It's "safe" consumption levels are pretty close to the dangerous ones, and due to the extremely addictive nature of it, it's more likely than other drugs to separate you cleanly into one of two categories: somebody who drinks only occasionally, or somebody who's a drunk.

I think it's left out of the 'drug war' and perceived as acceptable because it's the most damaging of the drugs. It's perceived by those that try to limit drug acceptance as, "The only chemical that extracts a worthwhile toll on the deadbeats that enjoy things like that".
